LESSON: WRITING 3.4.1 HANDWRITING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting, part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we write ascenders and descenders in words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.4.1 Handwriting together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: Learning independently as learners practise forming ascenders and descenders correctly as an aspect of good handwriting.

● Communication and collaboration: Writing skills are improved as the learner writes ascenders and descenders clearly and spell words correctly.

42

Values:
Responsibility: Ability to care for own and other’s property is enhanced as learner take care of digital devices when watching videos

Link to Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Learner Support Programmes : Peer education and mentorship is enhanced as the learner interpersonal relationships with others improve.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Mathematical Activities, Environmental Activities and Kenya Sign Language all emphasise good handwriting.

Suggested Learning Resources

Adapted course book, Chart, class readers, course books, flash cards, recording devices such as tablets, mobile phone, dictionary, internet, signed

audio-visual recordings
